page: Amazon Web Services i4i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 54 MB L3 cache.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a bundled local storage capacity of 937 GB on a single NVMe SSD, designed for low-latency, high-throughput operations. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and there are no GPUs.

Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Large-block memory read and write speeds are also in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput remains in the average tier.

Given the high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to the 4 vCPUs, the i4i.xlarge offers high resource density for storage-bound workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring fast local scratch space or caching layers rather than raw multi-core compute power. Appropriate workloads include transactional databases, NoSQL data stores, static web serving, and lightweight data processing tasks that benefit from local NVMe storage and 32 GB of RAM.
